title: Fluctuation-Driven Nonlinear Amplification of Quantum Statistics
authors: Yuewei Song, Zhenghe Zhou, Shuai Wan, Hecheng Wang, Jinpeng Li, Bowen Liu, Yinhai Li, Chunhua Dong, Guangcan Guo, Chong Wang, Zhiyuan Zhou, Baosen Shi
abstract: Photon statistics have moved to the forefront of modern optics, as intensity fluctuations and correlations shape multiphoton interactions and reveal information beyond mean-intensity measurements. Developing high-quality photon sources with pronounced correlations is a fundamental necessity in these fields. Here we demonstrate fluctuation-driven nonlinear statistical amplification of quantum light in spontaneous four-wave mixing using filtered amplified spontaneous emission (ASE). Extending the coherent-pump framework to fluctuating fields, we show how nonlinear weighting of pump intensity combines with bosonic bunching to amplify quantum statistics and reshape temporal correlations. In a SiN microring, ASE pumping increases the zero-delay unconditional second-order correlation from 2.01 to 7.58 and extends the Hanbury Brown--Twiss correlation time by a factor of approximately 2.4. The super-bunched quantum source nevertheless retains heralded single-photon behaviour with $g_H^{(2)}(0)\simeq0.04$, while the same ASE pump supports time--energy entanglement in a silicon waveguide with a raw Franson visibility of 89.84\%. These results establish driving-field statistics as a design dimension for quantum light, broadening the horizons for research into higher-order correlations and nonlinear physics.
summary: This paper demonstrates that using fluctuating pump fields, such as those from Amplified Spontaneous Emission (ASE), can nonlinearly amplify quantum photon statistics in spontaneous four-wave mixing within a SiN microring. The results show a significant boost in photon bunching compared to using a coherent pump, establishing that the statistics of the driving field is a crucial parameter for designing advanced quantum light sources.
main_problem: The paper investigates how fluctuations in the pump field can drive nonlinear amplification of quantum statistics in light generation, moving beyond standard coherent pumping models.
main_result: Using ASE pumping in a SiN microring, the unconditional second-order correlation ($g^{(2)}$) was significantly increased (from 2.01 to 7.58), demonstrating that pump fluctuations can enhance photon bunching while maintaining heralded single-photon behavior.
method: The study combines theoretical modeling of nonlinear interactions with experimental measurements using spontaneous four-wave mixing (SFWM) in a microring resonator.
model_or_system: The system is a SiN microring resonator undergoing SFWM, where the pump field is broadband Amplified Spontaneous Emission (ASE). The theoretical framework extends the coherent-pump model to include pump intensity fluctuations, leading to a nonlinear weighting of the generation rate ($\propto I_p^2(t)$).
key_observables: Unconditional second-order correlation ($g^{(2)}_u(0)$), Hanbury Brown–Twiss (HBT) correlation time, and time–energy entanglement (Franson visibility).
important_parameters:

u$) and the effective mode number ($M_p$) are key parameters governing the degree of statistical amplification.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the generated photon field is single-mode in some calculations, and the method relies on spectral filtering to extend the measurable coherence time.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the enhancement of HBT correlations due to pump fluctuations compared to coherent pumping, and show the dependence of statistical amplification on pump bandwidth ratios and effective pump mode numbers.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework for fluctuation-driven amplification, presenting experimental measurements comparing ASE vs. coherent pumping for $g^{(2)}$ and HBT correlations, and finally demonstrating entanglement generation using the fluctuating pump source.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems, as it shows that the statistics of the driving field itself can be engineered to enhance non-classical correlations in the generated quantum light, providing a new design dimension for quantum sources.
